drills.q: Name what Shor breaks and the one-line why.
drills.a: RSA (factoring), DH/ECDH and ECDSA/EdDSA (discrete log in abelian groups): all reduce to abelian hidden-subgroup problems that the QFT solves in poly time. Symmetric crypto untouched by Shor; Grover only halves it.

drills.q: Effective security of AES-256 under Grover, and the policy consequence?
drills.a: ~2^128 quantum operations: still safe. Consequence: standardize on AES-256 (and SHA-384 for long-lived hashes); do not replace symmetric primitives during PQC migration.

drills.q: Your nginx edge enables X25519MLKEM768 and handshake failures spike. Two likely causes?
drills.a: 1) Middleboxes/load balancers rejecting larger ClientHello (~2KB bigger). 2) Clients without hybrid group support hitting bad negotiation ordering. Fix LB firmware, keep X25519 ordered last as fallback, watch rollout telemetry.

drills.q: JWT auth uses RS256. What are your two realistic PQC paths?
drills.a: 1) Move to ML-DSA JOSE when supported end-to-end, accepting ~3.3KB signatures per token. 2) Refactor to opaque short-lived access tokens + introspection, signing only at issuance - shrinks signed surface and makes future rotations config-level.

drills.q: Why does SLH-DSA suit root CAs but not per-request API signing?
drills.a: Hash-based signatures reduce to conservative hash assumptions but cost 7-49KB per signature with slow hash-tree signing (hundreds/sec class). Root-of-trust cadence absorbs this; request-path workloads need ML-DSA's smaller/faster signatures.

drills.q: A PM says 'we'll migrate when quantum computers actually exist'. Rebut in two sentences.
drills.a: Harvest-now-decrypt-later means traffic recorded today is already compromised against a mid-2030s CRQC, so confidentiality has a deadline independent of hardware arrival. Enterprise migration takes 3-7 years; starting at Q-day guarantees being too late.

drills.q: What three artifacts prove PQC readiness to a federal customer?
drills.a: FIPS 140-3 validated crypto modules (140-2 historical since Sep 2026), CNSA 2.0 conformance statement mapped to acquisition dates (Jan 2027+), and a published CBOM/migration roadmap with algorithm inventory and dated milestones.

drills.q: Explain the LWE problem in one sentence and why it resists Shor.
drills.a: Recover a secret from noisy linear equations mod q (b = As + e): no abelian group structure means no reduction to hidden-subgroup/period-finding, so Shor's machinery does not apply; best attacks remain exponential/subexponential classical-and-quantum.

drills.q: Rank migration order: external TLS KEM, internal mTLS KEM, code signing, root CA rotation. Justify.
drills.a: 1) External TLS (HNDL-exposed now), 2) internal mTLS (same threat, more control), 3) code signing (no retro risk but long verification lifetimes), 4) root CA rotation (slowest cascade, plan last but start planning first).

drills.q: What does 'crypto agility' require architecturally, learned from SIKE/Rainbow?
drills.a: Algorithm choice behind configuration not code, dual-stack capability tested regularly, rollback rehearsals - because competition-grade algorithms died overnight to classical math, so the next transition must be a swap, not archaeology.
